phases.title: Phase 1 - Foundations
phases.description: What CI/CD is, how GitLab does it, and the five components every pipeline is made of: the file, pipelines, stages, jobs, runners. By the end you read a job log like a native and write a multi-job pipeline with artifacts and needs.

weeks.title: Week 1 - CI/CD, GitLab and your first pipeline
weeks.description: The XYZ team's problem, the vocabulary, an account and a project, and a pipeline you break on purpose.

lessons.title: Course introduction and the XYZ problem
lessons.summary: Why the XYZ team needs a pipeline, what CI, continuous delivery and continuous deployment mean, and how the eight weeks are laid out.

lessons.title: CI/CD basics and the anatomy of a pipeline
lessons.summary: Stages, jobs, runners and triggers - the shape every pipeline shares, and what a job really is.

lessons.title: GitLab account, group, project and the pipeline editor
lessons.summary: Set up gitlab.com, import the course resources and learn where pipelines and job logs live.

lessons.title: GitLab CI/CD core components
lessons.summary: .gitlab-ci.yml, pipelines, stages, jobs, runners and executors - and a job log read through all five.

lessons.title: Create and run a basic pipeline
lessons.summary: A three-job pipeline, a deliberate failure, Retry versus a new pipeline, and the five commands to run in any job.

weeks.title: Week 2 - Runners, stages, artifacts and needs
weeks.description: Who runs a job and how it is isolated; ordering work; passing files forward; and the DAG that frees jobs from the stage lock-step.

lessons.title: Types of runners and executors
lessons.summary: Instance, group and project runners; shell, docker and kubernetes executors; how the SaaS fleet works end to end.

lessons.title: Shared runners, before_script and scripts in files
lessons.summary: Run on shared runners, install tools honestly, and move long scripts into the repository.

lessons.title: Stages, stage vs stages, and dependent jobs
lessons.summary: Ordering with stages, what 'dependent' really means, and why stages are not free.

lessons.title: Artifacts - storing job data
lessons.summary: Hand files to later jobs and humans: paths, expire_in, dependencies, when:always - and why cache is a different thing.

lessons.title: The needs keyword and DAG pipelines
lessons.summary: Start jobs as soon as their dependencies finish; needs and artifacts; optional needs; when not to use it.

phases.title: Phase 2 - Pipeline configuration
phases.description: Controlling when and how jobs run: variables at every level, the predefined ones, rules at job and workflow level, schedules, resource groups, timeouts, images, services and parallel matrices.

weeks.title: Week 3 - Variables, rules, schedules and job controls
weeks.description: The week the pipeline learns to make decisions - and the two labs that explore every keyword so far.

lessons.title: Variables at every level, masking and protection
lessons.summary: Precedence from instance to job, File-type variables, what masking does and does not do, protected and scoped secrets.

lessons.title: Predefined CI/CD variables
lessons.summary: The variables every job starts with, and the patterns built on them.

lessons.title: Merge requests and rules at job level
lessons.summary: if, changes, exists, when and allow_failure - deciding whether a job exists, and with what.

lessons.title: workflow:rules, pipeline schedules and skipping pipelines
lessons.summary: Decide when a pipeline exists at all, run things at night, and skip a pipeline on purpose.

lessons.title: Resource groups, timeouts, images, services and parallel matrix
lessons.summary: One deploy at a time, bounded jobs, a database next to the tests, and N jobs from one definition.

phases.title: Phase 3 - Continuous integration
phases.description: A real application - the XYZ team's Node.js service - tested, reported on, built into an image, published to the registry and structured with templates, caches and merge request pipelines.

weeks.title: Week 4 - Testing the XYZ application
weeks.description: From a local npm test to a merge request that shows failing tests and coverage without anyone opening a log.

lessons.title: The XYZ Node.js application
lessons.summary: Run and test the app locally, and check the three things that make an app pipeline-able.

lessons.title: Designing the XYZ pipeline
lessons.summary: The stages, the decision behind every rule, the import and the skeleton you will fill in.

lessons.title: Unit testing in the pipeline
lessons.summary: npm ci, pinning the toolchain, a service for integration tests, and exit codes as the contract.

lessons.title: Test reports and coverage in the merge request
lessons.summary: JUnit, the coverage regex and Cobertura - failures and coverage where reviewers actually look.

lessons.title: Ignoring job failure and linting
lessons.summary: allow_failure and exit-code granularity, code quality reports, and the manual-gate trap.

weeks.title: Week 5 - Building, publishing and structuring
weeks.description: Images built in CI and published by SHA; caches that speed things up without breaking anything; templates, includes and merge request pipelines.

lessons.title: Building Docker images in the pipeline
lessons.summary: Docker-in-Docker, kaniko and the shell daemon; a reproducible, cached Dockerfile.

lessons.title: Publishing to the GitLab Container Registry
lessons.summary: Job-token login, a tagging strategy, build once and promote, cleanup policies.

lessons.title: Cache - and how it differs from artifacts
lessons.summary: Key on the lock file, policies, fallback keys, and why a missing cache must never break a job.

lessons.title: Templates: hidden jobs, extends, default and include
lessons.summary: Remove repetition and split the pipeline into files you can version and share.

lessons.title: Merge request pipelines, merged results and trains
lessons.summary: One pipeline per MR, testing the merge result, and the MR widget assembled.

phases.title: Phase 4 - Continuous deployment
phases.description: Environments GitLab can see, deployment over SSH with manual gates, the staging-to-production promotion path with protection and rollback, review apps per merge request, and deploying to Kubernetes.

weeks.title: Week 6 - Deploying to environments
weeks.description: The same image promoted through dev, staging and production - automatically, on a button, and behind a guard.

lessons.title: Environments and deployments
lessons.summary: environment:name/url/tier, environment-scoped variables, and the complete shape of a deploy job.

lessons.title: Deploying to a server over SSH with manual gates
lessons.summary: An SSH key as a File variable, verified host keys, job-token registry login on the server, and a blocking manual job.

lessons.title: Staging, production, protection and rollback
lessons.summary: The promotion path, protected environments and approvals, rollback versus revert, delayed jobs.

lessons.title: Review apps - an environment per merge request
lessons.summary: Dynamic environments, on_stop, auto_stop_in and the View app button.

lessons.title: Deploying to Kubernetes
lessons.summary: A kubeconfig variable versus the GitLab agent, kubectl and helm, and pulling from the registry.

phases.title: Phase 5 - Optimisation and security
phases.description: Pipelines that are fast, modular and safe: measuring the critical path, parent-child and multi-project pipelines, CI/CD components, the built-in security scanners, and the protections around the pipeline itself.

weeks.title: Week 7 - Faster, modular, safer pipelines
weeks.description: Less waiting, less duplication, fewer surprises - and the controls that make the pipeline itself hard to abuse.

lessons.title: Pipeline efficiency
lessons.summary: Measure the critical path; run less, start sooner, do less per job, split what is slow, fail fast.

lessons.title: Parent-child and multi-project pipelines
lessons.summary: trigger:include, strategy:depend, dynamic children generated by a job, and handing off to another project.

lessons.title: CI/CD components and the catalog
lessons.summary: Templates with typed inputs, versioned by tag and discoverable - include with a contract.

lessons.title: Security scanning in the pipeline
lessons.summary: SAST, secret detection, dependency and container scanning as includes, and how reports become gates.

lessons.title: Protecting the pipeline
lessons.summary: Protected refs, variables and environments, least-privilege tokens, CODEOWNERS on the pipeline, and fork safety.

phases.title: Phase 6 - Self-managed runners and Auto DevOps
phases.description: Running your own runners - install, register, tags, config.toml, executors, a hardened deploy runner - and Auto DevOps: the pipeline GitLab generates, how to customise it, and when to own your own.

weeks.title: Week 8 - Your own runners and Auto DevOps
weeks.description: The YAML does not change; where it runs does. Then the whole track, generated - and the capstone.

lessons.title: Installing and registering a self-managed runner
lessons.summary: gitlab-runner on Linux, authentication tokens, tags and scope.

lessons.title: Runner executors and config.toml
lessons.summary: concurrent and limit, privileged, volumes, pull policy, shared cache, and a hardened deploy runner.

lessons.title: Auto DevOps - the pipeline you did not write
lessons.summary: What Auto DevOps generates, what it needs, and when it pays.

lessons.title: Customising Auto DevOps
lessons.summary: Variables, including the template and overriding jobs, your own chart, and the line where it stops paying.

lessons.title: Capstone - the XYZ pipeline assembled, and what is next
lessons.summary: The final pipeline read back as a checklist of the eight weeks, and where to go from here.
